Use the cosine addition formula:
\[
\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{3}+\frac{\pi}{6}\right)=\cos\frac{\pi}{3}\cos\frac{\pi}{6}-\sin\frac{\pi}{3}\sin\frac{\pi}{6}
\]
\[
=\frac12\frac{\sqrt3}{2}-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\frac12=0
\]
This matches \(\cos(\pi/2)=0\).

Use the sine addition formula:
\[
\sin(x+\pi)=\sin x\cos\pi+\cos x\sin\pi
\]
Since \(\cos\pi=-1\) and \(\sin\pi=0\),
\[
\sin(x+\pi)=-\sin x
\]

questions.prompt: Derive \(\sin(2x)=2\sin x\cos x\) from the sine addition formula.
questions.answer:
Set both angles equal to \(x\):
\[
\sin(2x)=\sin(x+x)=\sin x\cos x+\cos x\sin x
\]
The two terms are equal, so
\[
\sin(2x)=2\sin x\cos x
\]

questions.prompt: Use \(\tan(a+b)=\frac{\tan a+\tan b}{1-\tan a\tan b}\) to find \(\tan75^\circ\).
questions.answer:
Use \(75^\circ=45^\circ+30^\circ\), with \(\tan45^\circ=1\) and \(\tan30^\circ=1/\sqrt3\):
\[
\tan75^\circ=\frac{1+1/\sqrt3}{1-1/\sqrt3}
\]
Multiply top and bottom by \(\sqrt3\):
\[
\tan75^\circ=\frac{\sqrt3+1}{\sqrt3-1}=2+\sqrt3
\]

Use the cosine difference formula:
\[
\cos(x-y)=\cos x\cos y+\sin x\sin y
\]
Substitute the given values:
\[
\cos(x-y)=\frac45\frac{12}{13}+\frac35\frac5{13}=\frac{48+15}{65}=\frac{63}{65}
\]
